samples.question: The top of the image shows four gray keys side by side; the bottom shows four colored sockets, one red, one orange, one green and one blue, in random order. Every key and every socket is a stack of four solid bars of equal thickness. Key bars start at the key's left edge and run rightwards; each socket is the same kind of stack drawn rotated by 180 degrees, so its bars end at the socket's right edge and its rows read in reverse order. A socket fits a key when the socket, slid onto the key without rotating it further, interlocks exactly: pairing the socket's bottom bar with the key's top bar, its next bar up with the key's next bar down, and so on, all four pairs must have the same combined bar length, so the two stacks together form a flush block with no gap and no overhang. Every key and every socket has the same total bar length, so size, ink and average bar length cannot identify the fit; only the arrangement of the bars can. Exactly one socket fits the key marked by the black triangle above it. What is the color of the socket that fits the marked key? Answer red, orange, green, or blue.
